policies.description:
Principle 2 — Data architecture and IT infrastructure. The bank shall establish and maintain integrated data taxonomies and architecture across the banking group, including metadata, single identifiers, and unified naming conventions for all legal entities, counterparties, customers, and accounts, so that risk data can be consistently linked and aggregated group-wide.

¶33: “A bank should establish integrated data taxonomies and architecture across the banking group, which includes information on the characteristics of the data (metadata), as well as use of single identifiers and/or unified naming conventions for data including legal entities, counterparties, customers and accounts.”
policies.title: Data Architecture and Integrated Taxonomy

policies.description:
Principle 3 — Accuracy and Integrity. The bank shall aggregate risk data in a manner that is accurate and reliable, with controls as robust as those applicable to accounting data; shall reconcile risk data to authoritative sources including the general ledger; and shall document all manual and automated aggregation processes with effective mitigants in place for any end-user computing reliance.

¶36: “A bank should aggregate risk data in a way that is accurate and reliable. Controls surrounding risk data should be as robust as those applicable to accounting data.”

¶36: “Risk data should be reconciled with bank's sources, including accounting data where appropriate, to ensure that the risk data is accurate.”

¶39: “Where a bank relies on manual processes and desktop applications (eg spreadsheets, databases) … it should have effective mitigants in place. … Supervisors expect banks to document and explain all of their risk data aggregation processes whether automated or manual.”
policies.title: Risk Data Accuracy and Integrity

policies.description:
Principle 4 — Completeness. The bank shall capture all material risk exposures — including off-balance-sheet positions — across every business line, legal entity, asset type, industry, and region, and shall measure and monitor completeness gaps, assessing their impact on the bank's ability to manage risk effectively.

¶41: “A bank's risk data aggregation capabilities should include all material risk exposures, including those that are off-balance sheet.”

¶41: “Data should be available by business line, legal entity, asset type, industry, region and other groupings, as relevant for the risk in question, that permit identifying and reporting risk exposures, concentrations and emerging risks.”

¶43: “Supervisors expect banks to produce aggregated risk data that is complete and to measure and monitor the completeness of their risk data. Where risk data is not entirely complete, the impact should not be critical to the bank's ability to manage its risks effectively.”
policies.title: Risk Data Completeness

policies.description:
Principle 5 — Timeliness. The bank shall ensure that risk data aggregation capabilities produce aggregate risk information on a timely basis to meet all risk management reporting requirements, with accelerated turnaround for critical risks during stress or crisis conditions.

¶44: “A bank's risk data aggregation capabilities should ensure that it is able to produce aggregate risk information on a timely basis to meet all risk management reporting requirements.”

¶45: “Banks need to build their risk systems to be capable of producing aggregated risk data rapidly during times of stress/crisis for all critical risks.”
policies.title: Timely Risk Data Aggregation

policies.description:
Principle 6 — Adaptability. The bank shall ensure that its risk data aggregation capabilities can respond to ad hoc requests, stress scenarios, and supervisory queries by producing novel aggregations on demand across key dimensions including country, industry, business line, and date, as of any specified reference point.

¶50: “a bank should be able to aggregate risk data quickly on country credit exposures as of a specified date based on a list of countries, as well as industry credit exposures as of a specified date based on a list of industry types across all business lines and geographic areas”
policies.title: Adaptability of Risk Data Aggregation

policies.description:
Principle 7 — Accuracy (reporting). The bank shall ensure that risk management reports are accurate and precise, supported by defined reconciliation processes between reports and underlying risk data, and by validation rules, edit checks, and exception reporting that confirm the integrity of reported figures.

¶52: “Risk management reports should be accurate and precise to ensure a bank's board and senior management can rely with confidence on the aggregated information to make critical decisions about risk.”

¶53: “To ensure the accuracy of the reports, a bank should maintain, at a minimum, the following: (a) Defined requirements and processes to reconcile reports to risk data.”
policies.title: Risk Report Accuracy and Reconciliation

policies.description:
Principle 8 — Comprehensiveness. The bank shall ensure that risk management reports cover all significant risk areas and all significant components of those risk areas, including dimensional breakdowns by single name, country, and industry sector for credit risk, so that the data elements feeding those reports are identified, classified, and demonstrably complete.

¶57: “Risk management reports should include exposure and position information for all significant risk areas (eg credit risk, market risk, liquidity risk, operational risk) and all significant components of those risk areas (eg single name, country and industry sector for credit risk).”
policies.title: Risk Report Comprehensiveness

policy_group.description: Policies and standards implementing the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Principles for effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting (BCBS 239) within the data catalog. Covers global and domestic systemically important banks across all legal entities, business lines, and geographies in both normal and stress/crisis conditions.
policy_group.title: BCBS 239

regulation.title: Principles for effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting

standard_attachment.$comment: DERIVED by alation_agent_kit.authoring.derive_attachment from each policy's principle. Not model output: it is a function of the policies and standards above, and asking a model for a derivable value invites a contradiction.

derived_requirements.description: Attests that this data element is governed by exactly one identifier per real-world object and that the authoritative register for that identifier is identified, per ¶33.

allowed_values: Yes – not yet documented in catalog
fields.name: Single authoritative source identified
Name and system reference of the authoritative identifier register

derived_requirements.name: Single Authoritative Identifier

derived_requirements.description: Attests that this identifier resolves consistently across all source systems that contribute to group-level aggregation, and that cross-reference mappings are current, per ¶33.

allowed_values: Mappings exist but not fully current
fields.name: Cross-system mapping status
Date of last cross-system mapping validation and reference to validation evidence

derived_requirements.name: Cross-System Identity Consistency

derived_requirements.description: Attests that metadata describing this data element — definition, format, owner — is recorded in the catalog and that naming conventions are applied consistently, per ¶33.

allowed_values: Complete – definition, owner, and format documented
fields.name: Metadata completeness in catalog
Any naming convention deviations identified and remediation plan reference

derived_requirements.name: Metadata and Naming Convention Compliance

standards.purpose: Without attestation that each critical data element has a single authoritative identifier and that cross-system identity mappings are current, there is no evidence that group-level aggregation is joining the correct population of records. Absent these answers, supervisors cannot confirm that the bank's taxonomy obligations under Principle 2 extend below the architectural design level to the actual data in production.
standards.scope: All critical data elements carrying entity, counterparty, or account identifiers: CDE-01 (Counterparty Identifier), CDE-02 (Legal Entity Identifier), CDE-10 (Source System Identifier).

derived_requirements.description: Attests that this data element is reconciled to the general ledger or designated system of record, and that the reconciliation frequency and materiality tolerance are defined and owned, per ¶36.

allowed_values: Reconciliation process defined but not yet run
fields.name: Reconciliation to system of record
Reconciliation frequency, tolerance, and reference to most recent reconciliation run

derived_requirements.name: Reconciliation to Authoritative Source

derived_requirements.description: Attests that any manual or end-user computing contribution to this element is identified, documented, and covered by effective mitigants, per ¶39.

allowed_values: No – fully automated feed from authoritative system
Yes – mitigants incomplete or out of date
fields.name: Manual or EUC input present for this element
Reference to mitigant documentation or explanation if no manual input

derived_requirements.name: Manual Process and EUC Control

derived_requirements.description: Attests that data quality monitoring for accuracy is active for this element and that an escalation path exists for identified failures, per ¶36.

allowed_values: Yes – active with documented escalation path
Yes – monitoring active but escalation path not documented
fields.name: Automated accuracy monitoring in place
Description of monitoring rule(s) and last exception raised with outcome

derived_requirements.name: Accuracy Monitoring and Escalation

standards.purpose: Without attestation that each data element is reconciled to an authoritative source and that any manual or EUC origin is identified and controlled, it is impossible to evidence whether an aggregate risk figure is arithmetically correct or whether it is the product of an unmitigated manual process. The absence of these attestations means neither the bank nor a supervisor can distinguish a reliable figure from an unverified one.
standards.scope: All critical data elements contributing to aggregate risk figures or subject to manual entry risk: CDE-03 (Gross Exposure Amount), CDE-09 (GL/System-of-Record Reconciliation Key), CDE-10 (Source System Identifier / Manual Override Flag).

derived_requirements.description: Attests that the proportion of material exposure records carrying a null value for this element has been measured and is within the required threshold, per ¶43.

allowed_values: Above 0% – within approved tolerance with documented exception
Above 0% – outside tolerance, remediation in progress
fields.name: Null rate on material exposure records
Count of null records found in most recent measurement run and date of run

derived_requirements.name: Null Population Coverage

derived_requirements.description: Attests that the population of records covered by this element includes off-balance-sheet exposures and spans all in-scope business lines, legal entities, and geographies, per ¶41.

allowed_values: Partial – some off-balance-sheet populations excluded with documented rationale
No – off-balance-sheet not yet in scope
fields.name: Off-balance-sheet exposures included in scope
Any known population gaps with impact assessment reference

derived_requirements.name: Off-Balance-Sheet and Full-Scope Inclusion

derived_requirements.description: Attests that where completeness is not 100%, the impact of the gap on the bank's ability to manage risk has been assessed and is not critical, per ¶43.

allowed_values: Gap identified – assessed as non-critical with documented rationale
Gap identified – criticality assessment in progress
Gap identified – assessed as critical, remediation mandated
fields.name: Impact of any completeness gap assessed
Reference to impact assessment document or remediation plan

derived_requirements.name: Completeness Gap Impact Assessment

standards.purpose: Without attestation that each data element has zero null values on material records and that the scope of material exposures is defined, it is impossible to determine whether an aggregate is computed over the full intended population. A completeness gap that is undetected or unmeasured cannot be assessed for impact, leaving the bank unable to meet the supervisory expectation in paragraph 43.
standards.scope: All critical data elements used as aggregation dimensions or exposure carriers: CDE-01 (Counterparty Identifier), CDE-02 (Legal Entity Identifier), CDE-03 (Gross Exposure Amount), CDE-04 (Risk Type Classification), CDE-05 (Business Line), CDE-06 (Geography / Country of Risk), CDE-07 (Industry / Sector Classification), CDE-08 (Position / As-of Date), CDE-11 (Transaction Currency).

derived_requirements.description: Attests that a production time window is defined for this element by risk type and reporting cycle, and that compliance with that window is monitored, per ¶44.

allowed_values: Yes – documented but not actively monitored
fields.name: Production SLA defined for this element
SLA value (time window), owning risk type, and reference to monitoring evidence

derived_requirements.name: Production SLA Definition and Compliance

derived_requirements.description: Attests that the ability to produce this element within an accelerated window during stress or crisis has been tested, per ¶45.

allowed_values: Yes – tested within last 12 months with documented result
Yes – tested but result not documented
fields.name: Stress/crisis production capability tested
Date of last stress test, accelerated window target, and outcome reference

derived_requirements.name: Stress and Crisis Production Capability

derived_requirements.description: Attests that every record for this element carries a valid, populated as-of date and that records from different business dates are not mixed into the same aggregate without explicit reconciliation, per ¶44.

allowed_values: Yes – 0 nulls confirmed in last measurement
fields.name: As-of date populated on all records
Any known instances of mixed-date aggregation and remediation status

derived_requirements.name: Temporal Integrity of Records

standards.purpose: Without attestation that each time-sensitive data element has a defined production SLA and that the SLA has been tested under stress conditions, the bank cannot demonstrate that its aggregation capabilities meet the timeliness requirements of Principle 5. An untested SLA is not evidence of capability; it is a statement of intent.
standards.scope: Critical data elements that carry temporal keys or contribute to time-critical aggregations: CDE-08 (Position / As-of Date). Also relevant to CDE-03 and CDE-01 where they feed credit, counterparty, trading, or liquidity aggregations subject to accelerated stress windows.

derived_requirements.description: Attests that this dimensional element is populated sufficiently and consistently to support on-demand country, industry, or business-line aggregation as of a specified date, per ¶50.

allowed_values: Yes – confirmed by test or recent ad hoc run
Partial – available for some date ranges only
fields.name: Element available for ad hoc aggregation as of any specified date
Reference to most recent ad hoc aggregation using this dimension, including date and scope

derived_requirements.name: Dimension Availability for Ad Hoc Aggregation

derived_requirements.description: Attests that the reference list governing valid values for this dimension (country codes, sector codes, business line hierarchy) is current and reflects the bank's live organisational and regulatory structure, per ¶50.

allowed_values: Current – reviewed within last review cycle
Stale – known out-of-date entries, remediation in progress
Unknown – last review date not recorded
fields.name: Reference list currency
Date of last reference list review and owner responsible for updates

derived_requirements.name: Reference List Currency

derived_requirements.description: Attests that this dimension can support stress-scenario aggregation runs (e.g. country shock, sector stress) within the timeframes required by the bank's stress testing programme, per ¶50.

allowed_values: No – not yet used in stress scenario
fields.name: Dimension included in at least one stress scenario aggregation in the last 12 months
Reference to stress scenario run and any dimension-coverage gaps identified

derived_requirements.name: Stress Scenario Slicing Readiness

standards.purpose: Without attestation that each aggregation-dimension element is populated, valid, and capable of supporting on-demand slicing by country, industry, and business line as of a specified date, the bank cannot demonstrate the adaptability capability required by Principle 6. Unattested dimensions leave the bank unable to evidence that an ad hoc supervisory request can be fulfilled.
standards.scope: Data elements that serve as aggregation dimensions enabling flexible slicing: CDE-05 (Business Line), CDE-06 (Geography / Country of Risk), CDE-07 (Industry / Sector Classification), CDE-08 (Position / As-of Date).

derived_requirements.description: Attests that a defined, documented reconciliation process exists between the reported value derived from this element and the underlying risk data, per ¶53.

allowed_values: Yes – documented but not consistently operated
fields.name: Reconciliation process defined and documented
Reference to reconciliation process documentation and owning team

derived_requirements.name: Report-to-Data Reconciliation Process

derived_requirements.description: Attests that the value of this element as it appears in risk reports has been confirmed as accurate and precise against the underlying data, per ¶52.

allowed_values: Yes – confirmed with documented minor exceptions
fields.name: Reported value confirmed accurate in last reporting cycle
Reporting cycle reference and any exception description with resolution status

derived_requirements.name: Reported Value Accuracy Attestation

derived_requirements.description: Attests that validation rules or edit checks are applied to this element prior to its inclusion in a risk report, providing a control against misstatement, per ¶53.

allowed_values: Yes – automated checks active and logged
Yes – manual checks applied and documented
fields.name: Validation rules or edit checks applied before report publication
Description of validation rule(s) applied and reference to last check output

derived_requirements.name: Validation Rules and Edit Checks

standards.purpose: Without attestation that the data elements feeding risk reports are reconciled to their underlying sources and that reconciliation processes are formally defined, the accuracy of any reported figure is unverifiable. A report that cannot be traced back to reconciled data cannot support the board and senior management reliance required by Principle 7.
standards.scope: Data elements that feed risk reports and are subject to report-level reconciliation requirements: CDE-04 (Risk Type Classification), CDE-09 (GL/System-of-Record Reconciliation Key). Also relevant to CDE-03 where it directly populates reported exposure figures.

derived_requirements.description: Attests that this data element is explicitly mapped to the risk report(s) it feeds and that the mapping confirms coverage of the required risk area or component, per ¶57.

allowed_values: Yes – mapping known but not documented in catalog
Partial – some reports mapped, others pending
fields.name: Element mapped to at least one risk report covering a significant risk area
Name(s) of report(s) this element feeds and the risk area each covers

derived_requirements.name: Risk Area Coverage Mapping

derived_requirements.description: Attests that this element supports the specific risk-report components named in Principle 8 — including single name, country, and industry sector for credit risk — and that its values are valid and populated for that purpose, per ¶57.

allowed_values: Partially – some values missing or invalid, documented gap
fields.name: Element supports required report component (single name, country, or sector) for credit risk
Specific component supported, coverage rate, and any known gap with impact

derived_requirements.name: Required Component Availability

derived_requirements.description: Attests that this element enables identification of concentrations or emerging risks within the scope of Principle 8, and that its use for concentration monitoring has been confirmed by the risk reporting team, per ¶57.

allowed_values: Yes – used in current concentration monitoring process
fields.name: Element actively used for concentration or emerging risk identification
Description of concentration measure(s) this element supports and owning risk function

derived_requirements.name: Concentration and Emerging Risk Visibility

standards.purpose: Without attestation that each dimensional element required for comprehensive risk reporting is populated and mapped to the correct report, the bank cannot demonstrate that its reports cover all significant risk areas and their components. An unmapped or unpopulated dimension silently removes an entire axis of a required report without any alert.
standards.scope: Data elements that constitute required report dimensions under Principle 8: CDE-04 (Risk Type Classification), CDE-07 (Industry / Sector Classification). Also relevant to CDE-06 (Geography) and CDE-05 (Business Line) as report coverage dimensions.
